dependent_variable.name: RPOJ
dependent_variable.definition: Risk premium (implied cost of equity less the 10-year US Treasury yield) inferred from the Ohlson–Juettner pricing relation. P0 is current price; eps1 and eps2 are one- and two-year-ahead EPS; dps1 is eps1 multiplied by current payout. The implementation uses the average of STG=(eps2−eps1)/eps1 and I/B/E/S five-year LTG as the short-term growth input, sets nominal perpetual growth gamma−1=rf−3%, and measures the RP on June 30. Current payout is dps0/eps0 when eps0>0; otherwise dps0/(0.06×total assets); payout ratios are winsorized to [0,1], held constant for future periods, and stock buybacks are ignored.
dependent_variable.formula: RP = re − rf; re = A + sqrt(A^2 + (eps1/P0) × (g2 − (gamma−1))); A = 0.5 × [(gamma−1) + dps1/P0]; g2_impl = (((eps2−eps1)/eps1) + LTG)/2; gamma−1 = rf − 3%; dps1 = eps1 × payout ratio.

evidence.quote: P0 = eps1/r_e + [eps2-eps1-r_e*(eps1-dps1)]/[r_e*(r_e-g_p)]. Substituting g_p=gamma-1 gives r_e = A + sqrt(A^2 + (eps1/P0)*(g2-(gamma-1)))
For implementation the authors use the average of forecast two-year growth and five-year growth as their short-term growth estimate.
The dependent risk premium is inferred cost of equity minus the prevailing10-year Treasury bond yield.
The inputs to the OJ model are P0, eps1, short-term growth g2, perpetual growth g, and dps1
We winsorize the payout ratios to lie between 0 and 1.
As in Gebhardt et al. (2001), we infer the risk premium on June 30 of each year.

review_notes: Source-first scope: the abstract says the authors compare RPOJ and RPRIV risk-premium measures in three ways (p. 1); Section 4.1 identifies Table 4 as the pooled full-panel regression family for their first evaluation (p. 14). Retain the final full-control rows in Panels B, C, and D for RPOJ, RPRIV1, and RPRIV2 as co-primary outcomes. Exclude Panel A's parameter-free E/P benchmark, reduced stepwise rows, Table 5's year-by-year stability fits, and later predictive/application analyses.

Table 4's note reports 15,872 observations for 1984–1998 (p. 17), while Table 1 reports 15,585 in its All row (p. 12) and Table 3 reports the same pooled count (p. 15). Record the direct Table 4 count for these pooled fits and flag the source discrepancy. Do not link the assigned sample ID: it describes the 15,585 observation Table 1/Table 4 Panel A sample.

The authors describe Table 4 as pooled regression but do not name the estimator. Table 4 reports t-statistics in parentheses without identifying the standard-error construction. Those details and the conflicting reported sample counts remain unresolved.

The Table 4 stepwise note omits EARNVAR from its list of controls, while the actual table has a populated EARNVAR coefficient column in each panel. Treat the list as an omission, not an assertion of absence, under source-specificity clarification 03; include EARNVAR as one RHS term and do not add component measures as standalone regressors.

EARNVAR is constructed with factor analysis; the source reports its three logged inputs and loadings, captured in the variable definition. It is not a regression fit. The recursively fitted regression controls beta and UNSYST are retained as supporting models.
